_about.what: How the market says a company's name, mapped to the securities code it files under. Platform curation, not a source field: no filing contains the word MUFG, JAL or Uniqlo, so this file is the only link between the name a user types and the filer. Generated initials (see app/aliases.py) cover the rest and are not repeated here.
rules: An alias earns a row only if today's substring search misses the company: the alias appears in neither the filed Japanese name nor the filed English name, and initials do not produce it.
One row per alias per securities code. An alias may name more than one company; matches are added to the search, never substituted for it.
A holding-company alias points at the LISTED parent, because that is the filer. SMBC and MUFG Bank do not file annual reports of their own; their parents do, and the row says so.
Former names are kept with a note. A code that stops existing is removed with a note in 'retired', never silently.
Nothing here changes a number. An alias only decides whether a company appears in a search box.
